interface.title: AquaScope Dashboard (v1.1.0, dashboard v1.0.0)
interface.stage_of_work: Data intake, quality control, exploratory analysis and hydrological / extreme-value analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: A Streamlit workspace where a hydrologist loads one discharge or water-quality dataset and then profiles it, cleans it, checks it against WHO limits, charts it and runs hydrology analyses on it (flow duration, baseflow separation, flow signatures, flood frequency), on pages that all share that dataset.

data.note: I uploaded water_quality_sample.csv (40 rows, 1 station, 4 parameters) and 01013500_daily.csv (3,650 days, 10 years of discharge_cms) through Collect Data > Upload file. In a second tab I loaded the built-in 'Demo: 40-yr streamflow' (14,610 rows) for Hydrology Lab. The workspace belongs to the browser session, so reloading a URL empties it (screens/029.webp).

tree.general: Bring in a monitoring record, check its quality, and get hydrological statistics and design values from it
tree.specific: Load a gauge or water-quality CSV into the AquaScope workspace, run EDA, WHO screening and cleaning, plot it, run baseflow, signature and flood-frequency analyses, and export the workspace dataset

features.name: Upload-and-profile card with dataset-aware next steps
features.general: Drop in a table, see an automatic profile (row count, sites, time span, completeness, quality score, detected roles of columns, guideline quick check), commit it as the working dataset, then jump to the analyses that suit its type
features.specific: Collect Data > Upload file: file drop zone, 'Use <file> as workspace dataset' button, Smart insights card (auto-detected time/discharge columns, WHO quick check) and Suggested next steps buttons that differ for water quality (quality alerts, baseflow, plot, map) and discharge (flood frequency, baseflow, plot, AI advice)
steps: Upload a CSV/JSON file
Read the Smart insights metrics and auto-detected columns
Expand the preview table
Press 'Use ... as workspace dataset'
Press a suggested next-step button to open the matching page
serves_tasks: Upload a tabular file and preview its auto-detected profile before using it
Set the working dataset used by all analyses

features.name: Shared workspace card with export and clear
features.general: A persistent side panel names the dataset every page is using (source, cleaned flag, size) and lets the user download it or empty it
features.specific: Sidebar Workspace card: 'Upload: water_quality_sample.csv (cleaned) · 40 rows × 4 cols', CSV button (aquascope_workspace.csv), Clear button; it shows 'Workspace: empty' with 'Load demo data' when empty
steps: Load or clean a dataset and watch the card update
Press CSV to download the current dataset
Press Clear to empty the workspace (tried only in the replay)
serves_tasks: Set the working dataset used by all analyses

features.name: Assess, recommend and apply a cleaning pipeline
features.general: Score data quality, get recommended cleaning steps pre-loaded into an ordered step picker, change the list, and apply it so the working dataset is replaced by the cleaned version
features.specific: Analyze & Clean tabs: EDA report (parameter stats with outlier counts, 'Distribution of' histogram) -> Quality assessment (completeness, duplicates, recommended steps) -> Preprocess (multiselect remove_outliers / resample_daily / remove_duplicates / fill_missing / normalize, Apply preprocessing). Applying dropped 5 of 9 columns and removed a real turbidity exceedance in this run
steps: Read the per-parameter statistics and outlier counts
Open Quality assessment to see the recommended steps
Open Preprocess; the recommended steps are already selected
Add or remove steps (added fill_missing)
Press Apply preprocessing; the workspace is marked '(cleaned)'
serves_tasks: See summary statistics per measured variable, with outlier counts and a distribution chart
Get an automatic quality assessment with recommended cleaning steps
Apply an ordered set of cleaning steps and replace the shared dataset with the result

features.name: Guideline-threshold exceedance screen
features.general: Compare each measured variable against a table of regulatory min/max limits and count the parameters that fail often (alert) or occasionally (warning)
features.specific: Quality Alerts: expandable WHO guideline reference (pH 6.5-8.5, DO >= 5, turbidity <= 5 NTU, nitrate <= 50, e_coli, arsenic, lead, mercury), metrics for parameters checked, Alerts (>10%) and Warnings (>0%), and a horizontal exceedance chart with a 10% alert line; on the raw sample, 1 warning (turbidity at 10.0%)
steps: Open Quality Alerts with an uncleaned water-quality dataset in the workspace
Expand the WHO guideline reference
Read the alert and warning counts and the exceedance bars
serves_tasks: Screen measured values against regulatory guideline limits

features.name: Chart-type switcher on the shared dataset
features.general: Pick a chart type and the columns it needs, then explore the interactive plot (hover, toggle a series from the legend)
features.specific: Visualize: Chart dropdown (Time series, Box plot, Correlation heatmap, Distribution, WHO exceedances, Station map, Flow duration curve, Hydrograph, ...) with matching column pickers (Column; Value + Group by); Plotly toolbar and legend toggling
steps: Choose a chart type
Choose the value column (and a grouping column for a box plot)
Click legend line symbols to hide series (toolbar zoom and image save not tried)
serves_tasks: Plot each variable over time and hide or show series

features.name: Baseflow separation with method switch and live parameters
features.general: Separate a time series into a slow background part and quick events with one of several digital filters, tune each filter's parameters with sliders, and read the resulting background fraction straight away
features.specific: Hydrology Lab > Baseflow Separation: Method radio Lyne-Hollick (alpha, number of passes) / Eckhardt (alpha, BFI_max) / UKIH (block size in days); BFI metric and a total-flow vs baseflow chart
steps: Choose the discharge column
Choose a method
Drag that method's parameter sliders
Read the BFI and inspect the baseflow line on the chart
serves_tasks: Split total flow into slow and quick components and compare separation methods

features.name: Flow duration curve with exceedance quantiles
features.general: Rank daily flows by how often they are exceeded, report median and low-flow quantiles, and draw the exceedance curve on a log axis
features.specific: Hydrology Lab > Flow Duration Curve (default analysis): Q50, Q95 and days-of-record metrics (8.197, 2.994, 14,610 on the demo) and a log-y FDC chart with Q50 and Q95 marked
steps: Choose Flow Duration Curve in Analysis
Choose the discharge column
Read Q50, Q95 and the record length
Inspect the log-scale exceedance curve
serves_tasks: Show how often each flow level is exceeded

features.name: Flow-regime signatures panel
features.general: Compute a standard set of flow-regime indices (mean flow, baseflow index, flashiness, high/low-flow quantiles and their ratio, peak month, seasonality) from one discharge series and list them in a table
features.specific: Hydrology Lab > Flow Signatures: metric cards (Mean flow, BFI, Flashiness (R-B), Q5/Q95 ratio, Q5 (high flow), Q95 (low flow), Peak month, Seasonality) and an 'All signatures' table. Caveat: Q5 and Q95 labels appear swapped (Q5 2.99 < Q95 16.61, ratio 0.2; FDC gives Q95 = 2.994)
steps: Choose Flow Signatures in Analysis
Choose the discharge column
Read the metric cards, checking Q5 against Q95
Read the All signatures table
serves_tasks: Compute a set of summary indices that describe the flow regime

features.name: Extreme-value fit with bootstrap return-level curve
features.general: Take yearly maxima from a series, fit a chosen extreme-value distribution, and get magnitudes for chosen return periods with bootstrap confidence bands, goodness-of-fit measures and observed plotting positions
features.specific: Extreme Events: Data source (Demo streamflow / Workspace dataset), Value column, Distribution (GEV / Log-Pearson III / Gumbel), Confidence level slider (0.80-0.99), Bootstrap samples slider (100-1000), Return periods multiselect; Run frequency analysis gives the goodness-of-fit metrics (AIC, KS p-value, n annual maxima, fitted parameters), a return-level curve with CI band and Weibull points, and a return-level table with lower and upper bounds. Only Gumbel finished in this run; GEV with 300 samples did not finish in several minutes
steps: Choose the data source and value column
Choose a distribution
Set the confidence level and number of bootstrap samples
Pick return periods
Press Run frequency analysis and read the fit metrics, curve and table
serves_tasks: Fit an extreme-value distribution to yearly maxima and read design magnitudes with confidence bounds for chosen return periods
